newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks add one percent as investors return.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks add one percent as investors return.

text.p: Swiss shares gained more than one percent in active trade on Wednesday as Novartis and Winterthur Insurance led the market higher, dealers said.
Market sentiment seemed to have changed as many wary investors who had stayed on the sidelines were now rushing back to the market, they added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index advanced 52.3 points, or 1.14 percent, to 4,634.9. The all-share Swiss performance Index was up 30.82 points to 2,929.78.
Novartis added 18 to 1,773 and Winterthur rose 48 to 1,049.
Winterthur shares were a big feature for most of the session after the insurance group said Thomas Wellauer, a senior manager at McKinsey Switzerland, was to succeed CEO Peter Spaelti.
Dealers said the news nourished speculation that the new CEO would seek closer cooperation with Credit Suisse Group.
CS Group rose 3.25 francs to 168.25 francs.
Other bank shares were also firmer as the market ignored weaker bonds.
Index heavyweights Novartis, Nestle, and Roche rose on foreign buying.
ABB and Georg Fischer were supported by generally rising demand for cyclical shares.
Second-tier shares saw good demand in Rieter, Belimo and in technology shares Logitech, Micronas and Stratec, which were high up on the winners list.

Technical problems at Switzerland's state telecomunications provider disrupted trading on the electronic Swiss Exchange by members connected to the bourse system via the Geneva access point, the bourse said.
It said the outage from 0830 to 0930 GMT affected 16 banks trading on the spot market and eight banks trading on Soffex.
Members were able to conduct limited amounts of business through other bourse members with access over Basle and Zurich.
